enzyme_name: Cob(II)yrinate a,c-diamide synthase (cobyrinic acid a,c-diamide synthetase)
organism_context: Salmonella enterica sv. Typhimurium LT2 CbiA (anaerobic B12 pathway); Pseudomonas denitrificans CobB is the aerobic hydrogenobyrinate counterpart
rationale: CbiA is a monomeric glutamine amidotransferase that amidates the c- then the a-carboxylate of cobyrinate at a single synthetase site; its only other chemistry is the glutaminase half-reaction of its GATase domain, which serves this same overall EC 6.3.5.11 activity rather than being an independent second activity, so it is scored monofunctional.
direction_note: The ATP- and glutamine-driven amidation is physiologically irreversible in the biosynthetic sense (cobyrinate -> cobyrinate a,c-diamide), which is the left-to-right direction as ModelSEED writes the equation, supporting the LLM's forward call over ModelSEED's reverse.

enzyme_name: Delta-6 enoate reduction step of bacterial bile-acid 7alpha-dehydroxylation (candidate catalysts BaiN, BaiCD, BaiH)
organism_context: Clostridium scindens and related gut Lachnospiraceae carrying the bai operon
rationale: KEGG flags R05836 as an 'incomplete reaction' with no EC and no KO (the redox partner is missing from the equation); the Delta-6 reduction that completes deoxycholate formation is attributed to bai-operon flavin-dependent oxidoreductases (BaiN/BaiCD/BaiH), but no protein has been shown to act on this 3alpha,12alpha-dihydroxy-Delta-6 substrate, so neither the catalyst nor its domain content can be settled.
direction_note: The gut-bacterial pathway runs reductively toward deoxycholate, i.e. 3alpha,12alpha-dihydroxy-5beta-chol-6-enoate + 2[H] -> deoxycholate, which is the forward (left-to-right) direction as written and matches the LLM call.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous (non-enzymatic) ring opening of strictosidine aglycone
organism_context: Catharanthus roseus and other monoterpenoid indole alkaloid producers
rationale: KEGG annotates R05844 as 'spontaneous (following EC 3.2.1.105 or R03820)': the aglycone released by strictosidine beta-glucosidase opens non-enzymatically to the dialdehyde, so there is no catalysing protein to classify as mono- or bifunctional.
direction_note: Being spontaneous and downstream of strictosidine beta-glucosidase, the flux runs aglycone -> dialdehyde, which is the forward direction as written; no enzyme constrains it to the reverse.

organism_context: Catharanthus roseus leaf idioblast/laticifer alkaloid metabolism
rationale: KEGG flags R05859 as an 'unclear reaction' with no EC or KO; only the upstream coupling of catharanthine and vindoline to anhydrovinblastine (class III peroxidase CrPrx1) is characterised, and the enzyme converting anhydrovinblastine to vinblastine remains unidentified even in the recent full-pathway reconstruction work.
direction_note: In planta flux runs anhydrovinblastine -> vinblastine (the forward direction as written here), so the LLM's forward call matches the biosynthetic sense.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous lactamisation of deacetylipecoside to demethylalangiside
organism_context: Alangium / Psychotria ipecacuanha isoquinoline (ipecac) alkaloid metabolism
rationale: KEGG annotates R05887 as 'spontaneous (following 4.3.3.4 or R05749)', i.e. the condensation product of the deacetylipecoside synthase step cyclises non-enzymatically with loss of methanol, so there is no catalysing protein to classify.
direction_note: A spontaneous lactamisation proceeds deacetylipecoside -> demethylalangiside, the forward direction as written, which is what the LLM called.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous lactamisation of deacetylisoipecoside to demethylisoalangiside
organism_context: Alangium / Psychotria ipecacuanha isoquinoline (ipecac) alkaloid metabolism
rationale: KEGG annotates R05889 as 'spontaneous (following 4.3.3.3 or R05750)' - the 1-alpha(S) epimer from deacetylisoipecoside synthase cyclises non-enzymatically - so no catalysing protein exists to classify.
direction_note: The spontaneous step runs deacetylisoipecoside -> demethylisoalangiside, i.e. the forward direction as written, matching the LLM call.

enzyme_name: none single - lumped multi-step conversion of deacetylisoipecoside to protoemetine
organism_context: Psychotria ipecacuanha (ipecac) root, emetine/cephaeline biosynthesis
rationale: KEGG has withdrawn R05891 entirely, and the transformation it encoded spans several enzymes (the beta-glucosidase Ipeglu1 plus reduction and the IpeOMT1-3 O-methyltransferases), each a separate monofunctional protein; there is no single catalyst for this lumped step.
direction_note: Ipecac alkaloid biosynthesis runs deacetylisoipecoside -> protoemetine -> emetine, so the forward direction as written is the physiological one.

organism_context: Psychotria ipecacuanha / Alangium ipecac alkaloid branch
rationale: KEGG flags R05894 as an 'unclear reaction' with no EC or KO; tubulosine arises from condensation of protoemetine with a tryptamine-derived unit, but no protein catalysing it has been reported, so no functionality call is possible.
direction_note: Protoemetine is the biosynthetic precursor of tubulosine, so flux runs in the forward direction as written, consistent with the LLM call.

enzyme_name: unidentified gut-bacterial urobilinoid reductase (BilR/BilV-family reductases act upstream)
organism_context: human gut Firmicutes (Clostridia) performing reductive bilirubin catabolism
rationale: KEGG R06257 carries no EC and no KO; BilR was only identified in 2024 as the bilirubin-to-urobilinogen reductase and the enzymes for the later urobilinoid reduction steps (i-urobilinogen -> L-urobilinogen/stercobilinogen) are explicitly still unknown, so no catalyst can be classified.
direction_note: Gut microbial urobilinoid metabolism is strictly reductive (progressive addition of hydrogens toward stercobilinogen), which is the forward direction as ModelSEED writes it, supporting the LLM call.

organism_context: Prochlorococcus spp., which use divinyl chlorophyll a; ChlG is conserved across cyanobacteria and plants
rationale: Chlorophyllide-to-chlorophyll esterification is performed by chlorophyll synthase ChlG (EC 2.5.1.62), a single-activity integral-membrane polyprenyl transferase; KEGG gives R06287 no EC/KO only because the phytyl-diphosphate partner is missing from the equation, so the enzyme assignment here is by chemistry.
direction_note: ChlG runs biosynthetically chlorophyllide -> chlorophyll (the forward direction as written); the de-esterification is run by a completely different enzyme, chlorophyllase, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call effectively attributes the reaction to the wrong protein.

enzyme_name: aphidicolan-16beta-ol synthase (ACS), a chimeric class II / class I diterpene cyclase
distinct_activities: syn-copalyl diphosphate synthase (class II, protonation-initiated bicyclisation; EC 5.5.1.14)
aphidicolan-16beta-ol synthase (class I, ionisation-initiated cyclisation with water capture; EC 4.2.3.42)
organism_context: Phoma betae (fungal aphidicolin cluster); the fused class II + class I architecture is characteristic of fungal diterpene synthases. The cluster's GGPP synthase (PbGGS) is a separate gene, so the bifunctionality is the two cyclase activities, not a prenyltransferase fusion.
rationale: ACS is one polypeptide carrying two catalytic domains and is annotated by KEGG under a single ortholog (K12928) with two ECs, 5.5.1.14 (GGPP -> syn-copalyl diphosphate) and 4.2.3.42 (syn-CPP -> aphidicolan-16beta-ol); the cloned cDNA alone reconstitutes both cyclisations.
direction_note: Both half-reactions are mechanistically irreversible (protonation-initiated cyclisation, then diphosphate ionisation with water capture), so this reaction can only run forward, syn-CPP -> aphidicolan-16beta-ol, as the LLM called it; the bifunctionality does not create a reverse-running domain.

distinct_activities: syn-copalyl diphosphate synthase (class II cyclase; EC 5.5.1.14)
aphidicolane class I cyclase (EC 4.2.3.42), which also releases aphidicol-16-ene by deprotonation instead of water capture
organism_context: Phoma betae; KEGG assigns R06314 to the same ortholog K12928 as the main ACS reaction
rationale: KEGG explicitly annotates R06314 with 'Aphidicolan-16beta-ol synthase, ACS' and ortholog K12928 carrying both EC 4.2.3.42 and EC 5.5.1.14; aphidicol-16-ene is an alternative deprotonation product of the same class I active site on the same bifunctional chain.
direction_note: Terpene-cyclase chemistry is irreversible toward the hydrocarbon product, so only the forward direction (syn-CPP -> aphidicol-16-ene) is physical, as the LLM called.

distinct_activities: syn-copalyl diphosphate synthase (class II cyclase; EC 5.5.1.14)
aphidicolane class I cyclase (EC 4.2.3.42), which also releases aphidicol-15-ene by alternative deprotonation
organism_context: Phoma betae; KEGG assigns R06315 to the same ortholog K12928
rationale: R06315 carries KEGG's 'Aphidicolan-16beta-ol synthase, ACS' comment and ortholog K12928 (EC 4.2.3.42 + 5.5.1.14), i.e. the same single bifunctional fungal diterpene cyclase; the 15-ene is a regiochemical variant of the terminal deprotonation.
direction_note: Class I cyclisation with diphosphate loss is irreversible, so only the forward direction (syn-CPP -> aphidicol-15-ene) is physical, matching the LLM.

enzyme_name: none single - lumped baccatin III -> paclitaxel conversion (BAPT, a C-2' hydroxylase, and DBTNBT)
organism_context: Taxus baccata / T. chinensis taxane biosynthesis
rationale: KEGG flags R06320 as an 'unclear reaction' with no EC: baccatin III -> paclitaxel needs at least three separate proteins (the BAHD acyltransferase BAPT, a P450 2'-hydroxylase, and the BAHD N-benzoyltransferase DBTNBT, EC 2.3.1.167), each individually monofunctional, so there is no single catalyst to classify.
direction_note: Every constituent step is either an acyl-CoA-driven acylation or a P450 oxidation, all physiologically irreversible toward paclitaxel, so the lumped reaction runs forward as written.

enzyme_name: cembrene (cembrane) synthase - a class I diterpene synthase; the specific protein is not established
organism_context: KEGG places the compound in plant/bacterial diterpenoid biosynthesis (map00904); tobacco CBTS and related cembranoid synthases make cembratrien-ol rather than cembrene itself
rationale: KEGG flags R06321 as an 'unclear reaction' with no EC and no KO; the chemistry (GGPP ionisation to a 14-membered cembrane macrocycle) is unambiguously a class I terpene synthase reaction, but no characterised protein producing KEGG C11893 cembrene is on record, so the catalyst - and therefore its domain content - is unknown.
direction_note: Class I terpene synthases are irreversible; diphosphate ionisation drives GGPP -> cembrene, the forward direction as written, so ModelSEED's reverse-only call is chemically backwards.

organism_context: Rhodococcus erythropolis DCL14, carveol/dihydrocarveol and limonene degradation
rationale: The activity defining EC 1.3.99.25 was detected only as 'an unknown cofactor-dependent carvone reductase' in R. erythropolis DCL14 cell extracts; the protein has never been purified, sequenced or cloned, so there is no evidence either way about a second catalytic domain.
direction_note: In the catabolic pathway the enzyme runs reductively, (4R)-carvone -> (1R,4S)-iso-dihydrocarvone, which is the forward direction as ModelSEED writes it (ModelSEED's display name 'Carvol' for cpd01220 is misleading - the compound is KEGG C01767, (4R)-carvone, C10H14O, and the 2 H+ represent the reducing equivalents).

organism_context: bacterial monoterpene (pinene/camphor) degradation, KEGG map00907; pathway seen physiologically in Pseudomonas and Nocardia but the ligase is unassigned
rationale: KEGG attaches only a generic EC 6.2.1.- to this substrate (C11944) with no gene, K number or characterised protein; the acyl-CoA synthetase acting on this acyclic monoterpenoid acid has never been purified or cloned, so no functionality call is defensible.
direction_note: Acyl-CoA synthetases of this class are pulled forward by ATP -> AMP + PPi and subsequent pyrophosphatase action, so the thioester-forming direction (forward as written) is the physiological one, supporting the LLM call.

organism_context: bacterial monoterpene (pinene/camphor) degradation, KEGG map00907; the trans isomer counterpart of rxn04272
rationale: As for the cis isomer, KEGG lists only a generic EC 6.2.1.- for C11943 with no gene or K number; the ligase has not been isolated, so there is no evidence about its domain content.
direction_note: ATP-dependent CoA ligation is driven forward by pyrophosphate release, so the acyl-CoA-forming direction (forward as written) is physiological.

organism_context: Mentha x piperita (peppermint) oil-gland secretory cells; menthol biosynthetic pathway
rationale: ISPR was cloned from a peppermint gland cDNA library and functionally expressed as a single-activity NADPH-dependent monoterpene double-bond reductase (short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase family); no second catalytic activity has been reported for it.
direction_note: ISPR is a committed NADPH-dependent reductive step of menthol biosynthesis (isopiperitenone -> (+)-cis-isopulegone), the forward direction as written; the oxidative direction is not physiological, so the LLM call is the biologically correct one.

organism_context: Mentha x piperita (peppermint) oil-gland secretory cells; EC 1.3.1.81
rationale: PGR was isolated as a single-activity NADPH-dependent monoterpene double-bond reductase; that it yields both (-)-menthone and (+)-isomenthone from the same substrate is stereochemical product partitioning at one active site, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: PGR runs reductively, pulegone + NADPH -> (-)-menthone, which is the forward direction as ModelSEED writes it (the 2 H+ stand in for the hydride plus proton); the reaction does not run oxidatively in vivo, so ModelSEED's reverse call is backwards.

organism_context: Mentha x piperita; EC 1.3.1.81, same protein as rxn04281 giving the (+)-isomenthone stereochemical outcome
rationale: The same cloned peppermint PGR produces (+)-isomenthone alongside (-)-menthone; a single reductase active site with two stereochemical outcomes is one catalytic activity, so the enzyme stays monofunctional.
direction_note: The physiological flux is the NADPH-dependent reduction pulegone -> (+)-isomenthone, the forward direction as written, so the LLM call matches the enzymology.

enzyme_name: (-)-alpha-terpineol synthase (KEGG also assigns 1,8-cineole synthase to this reaction)
organism_context: plant class I monoterpene synthases - e.g. (-)-alpha-terpineol synthase (EC 4.2.3.111, K18108) and 1,8-cineole synthase (EC 4.2.3.108, K07385), the latter characterised from Salvia officinalis
rationale: KEGG assigns R06421 to two single-domain class I monoterpene synthases, both of which carry one catalytic activity (GPP ionisation, cyclisation, water capture); generating several products from one active site is product promiscuity, which the protocol does not count as bifunctionality.
direction_note: Class I terpene synthases are irreversible: diphosphate ionisation and release drive GPP -> (-)-alpha-terpineol, the forward direction as written, so the LLM's call matches the mechanism and ModelSEED's reverse-only bound is unphysical.

organism_context: Streptomyces fradiae (tylosin, dTDP-L-mycarose branch); Saccharopolyspora erythraea EryBIII for the erythromycin mycarose
rationale: TylC3 was characterised as an S-adenosylmethionine-dependent C-methyltransferase that installs the C-3 methyl branch of L-mycarose with inversion of configuration, and KEGG's ortholog for this step (K13317, eryBIII/tylCIII) carries only EC 2.1.1.-; no second catalytic domain is reported. (KEGG has since re-drawn the step on the D-allose/D-glucose pair as R08933, but the catalysing enzyme family is the same.)
direction_note: SAM-dependent C-methylation is effectively irreversible (SAM -> SAH), so flux runs methyl-acceptor -> methylated sugar, i.e. the forward direction as written, supporting the LLM call.

organism_context: Streptomyces fradiae TylD (tylosin mycinose), Streptomyces sp. KCTC 0041BP GerKI (dihydrochalcomycin), Micromonospora griseorubida MydI (mycinamicin)
rationale: KEGG assigns R06438 to EC 1.1.1.364 and ortholog K13313 (tylD/gerKI/mydI), a single-activity NAD(P)H-dependent 4-ketoreductase of the short-chain dehydrogenase/reductase family that completes dTDP-6-deoxy-D-allose en route to mycinose; no second catalytic domain is described for these proteins.
direction_note: The biosynthetic flux is the NAD(P)H-dependent 4-keto reduction (dTDP-4-oxo-6-deoxy-D-allose -> dTDP-6-deoxy-D-allose), which is the forward direction as ModelSEED writes it; the dehydrogenase sense of the EC name is only nomenclature convention, so the LLM call is the physiological one.

enzyme_name: NDP-hexose C-3 ketoreductase of the 2,6-dideoxysugar pathway (OleW / EryBII / TylCII family, EC 1.1.1.384) - inferred, not confirmed
organism_context: Streptomyces antibioticus (OleW, oleandrose/olivose), Saccharopolyspora erythraea (EryBII), Streptomyces fradiae (TylCII) polyketide deoxysugar pathways
rationale: KEGG has withdrawn R06441 and leaves C11932 orphaned with no reaction, EC or KO; by chemistry the step is the reduction of a 2,3-dehydratase product (dTDP-2,6-dideoxy-hex-2-enos-4-ulose) corresponding to the C-3 ketoreductase of the dTDP-L-olivose/oleandrose/mycarose modules, but no protein has been tied to this specific L-erythro substrate pair, so the catalyst and its domain content stay unresolved.
direction_note: The deoxysugar pathway runs reductively through this step toward the dTDP-2,6-dideoxy sugar, i.e. the forward direction as written, which is what the LLM called.
